title: S&P 500 Fell 9% and Rebounded, as a BTIG Strategist Expected
summary: The S&P 500 fell roughly 9% after November 12, then rebounded. How BTIG strategist Jonathan Krinsky's calls tracked the swing, and what his record shows.
body_markdown:
## Half of Stocks Stayed Above Their 50-Day Averages


Krinsky also noted that the selling had been narrower than at past lows. About half of S&P 500 stocks were still above their 50-day moving averages in the week to November 20, while at the lows of pullbacks of 8% or more since 1997, the median reading was 11%.


[Apple (AAPL)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/aapl/) was about 2.6% below its 52-week high of $360.83 at the time of his note. By his count, genuine S&P 500 bottoms since 2015 came with a median Apple[drawdown](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/what-is-drawdown-meaning-risks-and-example/) of 23%.


## CXO Advisory Grades Krinsky 27% Right Since 2022


Two weeks of accurate calls are one stretch in a longer record.[CXO Advisory](https://www.cxoadvisory.com/gurus/jonathan-krinsky/) found that 16 of Krinsky's 59 graded market calls since 2022 were right as of November 23, 2026, or 27%. That gives him a grade of F and ranks him 17th of the 21 forecasters the site gives a letter grade.


His most recent graded call on the site, a bearish one from August 5, 2026, was marked right when it came due on November 5, with the S&P 500 down 4.8% over that span.
